safe_steps: Stop the cycle if the appliance behaves abnormally.
Switch the appliance off.
Disconnect power only if safe and accessible without contact with water or damaged equipment.
Do not remove panels, handle wiring or bypass safety interlocks.
Check the exact model number and matching manufacturer's manual.
records.source_note: Sources show codes/actions are model-specific; they do not establish the meaning of E21 for an unidentified washer.

records.documentation_scope: general manufacturer guidance, not exact-model diagnosis
probable_causes: Temperature controls may be set incorrectly.
Internal air vents may be obstructed by food packages.
Frequent door opening or a large recent load may temporarily affect internal temperature.
A recently installed appliance (purchased 3 days ago) may need up to 24 hours to stabilize operating temperature.
safe_steps: Check the temperature setting without opening service panels.
Check that food packages do not block visible internal air vents.
Ensure doors close fully and seals are unobstructed.
For a new installation, allow adequate time between door openings for temperatures to recover.
If cooling does not recover, arrange qualified service.
stop_conditions: Smoke, burning smell, sparks, damaged power cord, water near electrical components or an immediate electrical hazard: stop and seek qualified help.
Do not remove panels, handle refrigerant or work on electrical components.
records.source_note: General manufacturer guidance, not an exact-model diagnosis.

records.documented_error_meaning: Drain filter or waste pump may be blocked or drain hose kinked.
probable_causes: Food debris clogging the coarse/fine cylindrical filter.
Sink connection or garbage disposal knockout plug restriction.
Drain hose kinked behind the cabinet.
safe_steps: Turn off the dishwasher and disconnect power before inspecting.
Remove lower rack and twist filter counterclockwise to remove.
Rinse filter assembly under running tap with a soft brush.
Check for standing water under the filter cover; remove any visible glass or seeds.
Reinsert and lock the filter before running a short test cycle.
stop_conditions: Electrical burning smell, scorched cord, or water leaking onto flooring: stop and seek service.
Never disassemble the pump impeller housing with sharp tools.

probable_causes: Heavy lint accumulation in the lint trap or external vent duct.
Crushed or kinked flexible exhaust foil behind the unit.
Outdoor vent hood flapper stuck closed.
safe_steps: Clean the lint screen thoroughly before every single load.
Pull dryer forward slightly to inspect rigid exhaust pipe for crushing.
Verify outdoor exhaust flapper opens freely when air blows out.
Allow dryer to cool down completely before restarting.
stop_conditions: Smell of burning lint or smoke: stop immediately, disconnect power/gas, and call for service.
Do not operate dryer without the lint screen firmly in place.

probable_causes: Air filters dusty and restricting intake airflow.
Remote control set to Fan or Dry mode instead of Cool mode.
Direct sunlight on indoor unit or windows open in room.
Outdoor condenser unit obstructed by leaves or debris.
safe_steps: Check remote control mode is set to 'Cool' with setpoint lower than room temperature.
Open front panel, slide out washable mesh filters, rinse under water, and let dry completely.
Clear any furniture, drapes, or objects blocking the front air louvers.
Ensure outdoor unit has at least 12 inches of clear clearance around coils.
stop_conditions: Refrigerant hissing sound, burning electrical smell, or ice buildup on coils: stop and contact HVAC technician.
Do not spray water directly into electrical control boxes.

records.documented_error_meaning: Inverter power supply or magnetron circuit issue.
probable_causes: Door interlock switches not fully engaging.
Power level inadvertently set to 0% or Kitchen Timer mode used.
High voltage inverter failure.
safe_steps: Verify the door closes firmly and latches click on both upper and lower catches.
Check that display shows 'Cook' rather than 'Timer'. Test with 1 cup of water for 30 seconds at 100% power.
Unplug microwave for 1 minute to reset electronic microprocessor controls.
stop_conditions: High voltage hazard: NEVER remove outer metal cabinet of microwave oven. Internal capacitor retains lethal voltage even when unplugged.
Sparks, arcing, or burnt waveguide cover: stop immediately and seek authorized technician.

probable_causes: Bake rack placed on incorrect level for recipe.
Aluminum foil lining oven bottom blocking convection heat flow.
Door gasket damaged allowing hot air escape.
safe_steps: Ensure baking pans have at least 1.5 inches of air space between each other and oven walls.
Remove any aluminum foil or silicone mats from the oven cavity floor.
Inspect rubber door seal around cavity perimeter for tears or loose corners.
Preheat fully until oven indicator confirms target temperature.
stop_conditions: Gas odor, smoke, or error F-codes: shut off oven immediately and call certified technician.
Do not touch heating elements or attempt to service internal wiring.

probable_causes: Sediment or carbon pre-filter clogged by particulate matter.
Inlet water valve turned off or low household water pressure.
Storage tank air bladder pressure low.
safe_steps: Check that cold water supply angle valve to purifier is fully open.
Verify inlet tube is not bent or pinched.
Check pre-filter bowl for visible silt or sediment discoloration.
If filters have been in use for over 12 months, schedule replacement.
stop_conditions: Electrical shock risk: unplug from wall outlet immediately if water drips near power adapter.
Do not operate without genuine certified filtration cartridges.

probable_causes: Dust bin filled past MAX line.
Washable HEPA filter clogged with fine gypsum or carpet powder.
Blockage in cleaner head neck, wand tube, or bin inlet.
safe_steps: Empty clear dust bin into trash can when debris reaches MAX marker.
Unclick wand and look through tube against a light to spot clogs.
Twist off rear filter, wash in cold running water without detergent, and air-dry for at least 24 hours.
Remove brush roll end cap and cut away tangled hairs.
stop_conditions: Do not vacuum liquids or damp carpets with dry-only vacuum cleaner.
Never use vacuum without completely dry filter installed.

probable_causes: Circuit breaker for water heater tripped in main electrical panel.
High-limit safety switch (red reset button) tripped on upper thermostat.
Recent heavy hot water demand (multiple showers, laundry) depleted tank.
safe_steps: Check main home breaker panel to confirm 240V double-pole breaker has not tripped.
Wait 30-45 minutes after heavy usage for tank recovery.
Check temperature dial setting (120°F / 49°C recommended for safety and scald prevention).
stop_conditions: Scald and electrocution hazard: do NOT remove thermostat covers while power is connected.
Active water leaking from tank body or pressure relief valve: turn off power and main water valve and call licensed plumber.

probable_causes: Input source set to wrong HDMI port.
HDMI cable loose or damaged between cable box/console and TV.
Display panel power saver / screen off mode engaged.
safe_steps: Press 'Input' or 'Source' button on remote to toggle through HDMI 1, 2, 3, 4.
Reseat HDMI cables firmly at both ends.
Perform soft reset: unplug TV power cord from wall outlet, wait 60 seconds, press power button on TV for 10 seconds, then plug back in.
stop_conditions: Cracked glass, blinking red standby LED (error code), or smoke: unplug immediately and contact authorized service.
Never open TV back casing; high voltage components inside.
